title: Second Round of US-Backed Government-Opposition Transition Talks Opens in Caracas
detail: The government and an opposition delegation opened a second round of US-backed political transition talks at the Hotel Meliá Caracas on September 17, after 17:30 local time. The government side was again led by National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez; the opposition delegation was again led by Dinorah Figuera, who returned to Caracas on September 13 ahead of the session. This round is billed as covering civil and political guarantees, freedom of expression, a full renovation of the Supreme Tribunal of Justice, lifting international sanctions (a government priority), and further releases of political prisoners. The first round, held August 6–12, produced two agreements: a full TSJ renewal process and recovery of Venezuelan reserves held at the Bank of England. As before, María Corina Machado and the majority opposition leadership are not at the table; Figuera said an announcement on any agreements reached could come once this week's discussions conclude.

media.caption: Dinorah Figuera and Jorge Rodríguez led the government and opposition delegations into a second round of transition talks

title: Trump Plans First-Ever Meeting With Delcy Rodríguez on UN General Assembly Sidelines
detail: Axios reported September 17 that President Trump is planning a first-ever face-to-face meeting with Venezuelan Interim President Delcy Rodríguez, potentially as early as the following Tuesday, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York (Sept 22–28). A Trump adviser told Axios: 'Venezuela is without a doubt the president's top success, and Delcy is a key to that,' noting Rodríguez's cooperation with Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on normalizing relations, including the recent oil agreement. Trump had signaled openness to the idea on September 14, telling reporters 'I may be, I may be' when asked about meeting Rodríguez. A US administration source cautioned no final decision has been made, and some in Trump's circle worry a meeting could undermine Rodríguez domestically by making her appear to be an American proxy. The encounter would come near the New York-area facility holding Maduro, who faces narco-terrorism charges; potential agenda items include sanctions, election timing, and continued security cooperation. The Venezuelan exile community in South Florida has voiced growing unease that neither Trump nor Rubio has publicly demanded Rodríguez schedule elections.

media.caption: Trump said 'I may be, I may be' when asked about a UN meeting with Delcy Rodríguez
